member.name: T:Lumio.GameRuntime.Coordination.HostVoxelWorldAdapter
member.summary: ADR-119 binding context ownership (R-00727): the block-type → block-entity-type policy is the only thing gameplay supplies. Runtime derives every live candidate of a declared type from itself and is the sole writer of the native candidate list — there is no second entry point that accepts an explicit entity list, so a stale gameplay snapshot can never race Runtime's own view. This file also implements , the Section-level committed binding table read consumed by Runtime's own Section subscription projection (R-00726).
Bounded staging over a caller-owned Native voxel world; Native owns historical receipts.

Thin owner-thread wrappers over the four ADR-119 Section residency ABI slots (R-00727): voxel_section_durability_ack_v1, voxel_section_unload_v1, voxel_section_release_v1 and voxel_section_load_v1. This file does not decide when a Section should load, unload, be acked or be released, and does not enforce Authority/Client role — Native's own role check (InvalidArgument for the wrong role, see voxel_residency rules) is the enforcement point. Deciding the sequence, timing and role is Section residency orchestration and belongs to R5, not this card.

Every must resolve through to a type declared in (ADR-119 决策 1 / 6); anything else — an unresolvable wire name or a CLR type without [BlockEntity] — is rejected before any native call.

member.name: M:Lumio.GameRuntime.Coordination.HostVoxelWorldAdapter.RefreshBindingContext
member.summary: Re-derives the native binding candidate list from every live entity of a policy-declared type and pushes it to Native (the only writer, ADR-119). Call again whenever the live candidate set may have moved after the last push — in particular after a Section load/restore hydrates its entities ("refreshes the binding context before the next Tick", voxel_section_load_v1 rules); already does this for its own call, but a residency orchestrator that hydrates entities separately (R5) must call this again once that hydration is done.

member.name: M:Lumio.GameRuntime.Coordination.HostVoxelWorldAdapter.TryReadSectionBindings(System.UInt64,System.Collections.Generic.IReadOnlyList{Lumio.GameRuntime.Ecs.SectionBindingEntry}@,System.UInt64@)
member.remarks: Rejects a non-owner-thread caller before touching Native; never caches — every call re-reads Native's committed table (voxel_section_binding_read_v1 is the only truth). Both the authority (Runtime's own Section subscription projection, R-00726) and a predicting client's own gameplay/GAS code ( non-null) may call this: Native accepts both worlds (R-00725, R-00768) and each call only ever reads 's own world — a client never reaches another connection's data through it, and a client's bounded prediction session is a separate Native construct layered on top, so an open session does not block this read of the base world's committed table (ADR-119 决策 2: "位置只有一个来源：绑定表，两端同一份"). An unparseable entity id from Native is a fault — this method does not catch 's exception, so it propagates.

member.name: E:Lumio.GameRuntime.Coordination.HostVoxelWorldAdapter.DigApplied
member.summary: Raised once per dig, synchronously inside TickPhase.VoxelCommit (from ), after Native has applied the transaction. Observe-only (tick.md §3 rule 5, Owner 2026-09-18): subscribers may read and record, nothing else. While a subscriber runs the bound is in an observe-only window: World.Commands.Create / QueueDestroy / local create-destroy and every Sync<T>.Value (or Sync container) write throw. Do not queue structural orders, effect orders or any other business settlement here. When staging a dig, retain pending settlement and read in phase 3 or 4 of a later frame. Settle only successful results; discard refused pending work without charging, clearing reserves or creating drops. A business refusal is not a fault. Any subscriber exception (including rejection of a forbidden callback write) is recorded as a , faults this adapter and propagates out of , so the whole tick fails as VoxelCommit ProcessFault. No production code in this repository subscribes today; when a host does, Prime cannot see the subscriber ahead of time (it is registered at runtime, after Bind) — Tick path warmup coverage tracked in Coordination.Tests.TickPathCallbackCompletenessTests (R-00763 follow-up 1).

member.remarks: is randomized per process and only 32 bits wide, so the same txn id produced a different native number on every replay and two different ids collided far too easily (R-00469 §f). This derivation is a pure function of the contract id: identical across processes, machines and replays, and 64 bits wide.
